seo_title: Sanganeri vs Bagru vs Dabu Print – Jaipur Block Print Guide
seo_description: Learn the difference between Sanganeri, Bagru and Dabu block prints from Jaipur, and how to identify real hand block printed kurtis.
body:
Jaipur is famous for block printing, but not all block prints are the same. Here is a simple guide to the three prints you will see most often.

## Sanganeri print

From Sanganer, near Jaipur. Fine floral buttis and creepers, usually on a white or light background with soft colours. Elegant and perfect for daily wear and office kurtis.

## Bagru print

From the village of Bagru. Earthy colours like rust, black, mustard and indigo, often on an off-white or natural background. Bolder and more rustic than Sanganeri.

## Dabu print

Dabu is a mud-resist technique. A paste of clay is printed on the fabric, then the fabric is dyed – often in indigo. The areas under the mud stay light, which creates a slightly cracked, handmade look.

## How to spot real hand block printing

- Small variations in the print – no two repeats are exactly the same
- Slight overlap or gaps where blocks meet
- The print looks softer on the back of the fabric
- Natural, slightly uneven colour

These small imperfections are not defects. They are the signature of a handmade product.

## Caring for block printed clothes

Wash separately in cold water the first few times, use mild detergent and dry in shade. This keeps colours bright for longer.
